newsitem.title: MEXICO: Nevada Goldfields eyes IPO, Mexico bolsa listing.
newsitem.headline: Nevada Goldfields eyes IPO, Mexico bolsa listing.

text.p: -Consolidated Nevada Goldfields Corp. is seeking a combined global IPO and Mexican Stock Exchange listing, the president and CEO of Denver- based mining company said here Tuesday.

"We are in the process of listing the company on the bolsa in Mexico City," Geoffrey Hoyl told Reuters in a brief interview Tuesday, adding the idea was to combine a modest IPO offering of around $5 million with a Mexican listing.
"The sooner the better is always my take in these circumstances," he added when questioned on the timescale of the IPO and listing.
Hoyl said he was going for talks with officials at the Mexican Stock Exchange soon and would also be meeting with financiers at Grupo Financiero Inverlat to discuss details.

Nevada Goldfields is a gold, silver, copper and barite mining company which operates the Pachuca, Baztan, Magistral del Oro and Barita de Sonora mines in Mexico and the Nixon Fork and Aurora mines in the United States.
The Mexican properties were acquired last year for around $65 million from Grupo Real Del Monte SA, a unit of the closely- held Grupo Acerero del Norte.
Nevada Goldfields already trades on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the German exchanges in Stuttgart, Frankfurt and Berlin.

It counts amongs its resources proven and probble reserves of approximately 600,000 ounces of gold, 47 million ounces of silver, 28 million pounds of copper and 4 million tonnes of barite, a mineral used in the petroleum industry.
